Session 2 Facilitator Rehearsal Run Sheet

Make evidence earn the decision

Version: 2026-08-23 Format: 135-minute live cohort session Cohort: up to 10 PMs with approximately 2-6 years of experience Deck: 19-page HTML/PDF facilitator deck Preparation: the Session 2 pre-read is not released in the current site build; do not treat the live deck as its substitute

This is a rehearsal document, not a teleprompter. It is intentionally fuller than the spoken delivery. Rehearse the argument, case logic, questions, transitions, and recovery language; then teach in your own voice.

The facilitator's job

By the end of the session, learners should be able to update a product decision without confusing:

  1. evidence volume with decision relevance;
  2. a metric name with a valid product definition;
  3. a coherent synthesis with a traceable belief;
  4. an observed estimate with the unknown underlying effect; and
  5. statistical output with product significance or authority to launch.

The governing message is:

Evidence is valuable when it can change a defined decision, retains the boundary of what it can establish, and produces an accountable belief update.

Session 1 established the decision, current view, and weakest consequential claim. Session 2 begins from that claim. Do not let the live session become a survey of research methods, analytics, or statistics. Every concept must return to the same question: what can this evidence justify for this decision?

Source and accuracy stance

  • The required teaching spine is Reforge-derived and reorganized into the course's own evidence-to-decision chain.
  • The Noted product is real; Week 2 interviews, support tags, analytics, and pilot results are constructed for practice.WN-02
  • The statistical interpretation deliberately corrects unsafe simplifications in the source material. A p-value does not measure the probability that a hypothesis is true, and statistical significance does not establish effect size or product importance.S2-SN-10
  • A non-significant result does not establish no effect. It may remain compatible with effects that matter to the decision, depending on the design and uncertainty.S2-SN-12
  • The numerical example is illustrative and should test supervision and decision judgment, not arithmetic speed.

Before learners arrive

  • Open the HTML deck and verify arrow-key navigation and fullscreen mode.
  • Keep a visible six-minute timer ready for slides 8, 13, and 17.
  • Prepare one capture surface with five headings: claim, can establish, cannot establish, belief update, and decision change.
  • Keep the Week 1 decision boundary available, but do not reopen prioritization. The shared route continues with the meeting-meaning claim so the evidence can accumulate.
  • Ask learners to keep their answer private until the timer ends. Select two or three responses yourself; there is no peer critique requirement.
  • Do not reveal the model interpretation before individual work. The purpose is to observe how learners supervise evidence, not whether they can repeat a statistical phrase.
  • Treat every Week 2 case observation and number as constructed unless the provenance note says otherwise.WN-02

Facilitation stance

Use five moves throughout:

  1. Return to the decision. Ask: "Which choice could this evidence change?"
  2. Name the evidence job. Ask: "What can this source establish that the others cannot?"
  3. Inspect observability. Ask: "Does the captured event represent the behavior in the claim?"
  4. Preserve the strongest contradiction. Ask: "What is the most serious evidence against this abstraction?"
  5. Require an update. Ask: "Did the belief strengthen, weaken, narrow, reframe, or remain unchanged—and what happens to the decision?"

Useful recovery phrases:

  • "That method can produce information. What decision-relevant uncertainty will it reduce?"
  • "You have named the metric. Now define the behavior, actor, denominator, and window."
  • "A dashboard displaying the event does not establish that the event means what you think it means."
  • "Show me the observation underneath that theme."
  • "Show me the counterevidence the theme does not explain."
  • "The result missed a threshold. Which effects are still compatible with the evidence?"
  • "Statistically clear is not the same as worthwhile. What is the product threshold?"

Avoid these phrases:

  • "Experiments are the strongest evidence."
  • "The metric is standard."
  • "The synthesis says..." without source lineage.
  • "The data is flawed, so we cannot use any of it."
  • "The test proved..."
  • "There is no effect" based only on non-significance.
  • "We should keep running it until it becomes clear."

Slide-by-slide rehearsal script

Slide 1 - Make evidence earn the decision

Time: 4 minutes Job: Reframe evidence work as decision work rather than information production.

Rehearse

"Session 1 ended with a decision, a current product view, and a weakest consequential claim. Session 2 does not begin by asking which research method we like. It begins by asking what evidence could change that decision."
"The common failure is not lack of data. It is producing research, analysis, or experiment results that never had a clear decision job. The packet gets larger; the decision remains implicit."
"Today we will make three moves. Choose evidence that can answer the claim. Turn mixed observations into a defensible belief. Then interpret measurement without manufacturing certainty."

Ask

"Think about the last research or analytics readout you attended. What product decision changed because of it?"

Do not collect answers. Let the gap between information and action become visible.

Transition

"We are building one update, not three evidence artifacts. Here is the chain."

Slide 2 - One traceable belief update

Time: 6 minutes Job: Establish the cumulative logic and reuse the Session 1 teach-decide-debrief contract.

Rehearse

"The first move is an evidence plan: state the claim, choose sources for specific jobs, define the metric in product terms, inspect observability, and decide when another evidence cycle stops being valuable."
"The second move is a belief update: travel from observations to patterns and mechanisms, then back down to support, contradiction, segments, and flaws."
"The third move is a measurement boundary: distinguish the observed estimate from the unknown effect, compare it with a product threshold, inspect error consequences and test integrity, then choose an action."
"The output is one record. Another PM should be able to see why the belief changed, why it did not change further, and what the decision now requires."

Listen for

If learners expect a methods class, correct early:

"You are not being assessed on naming the ideal research technique or calculating a statistic. You are being assessed on whether the evidence fits the decision and whether your conclusion respects its limits."

Transition

"Here is the Week 2 evidence release. Resist the urge to synthesize it while I read it."

Slide 3 - Mixed Noted evidence release

Time: 6 minutes Job: Make evidence heterogeneity and provenance visible before teaching the method.

Rehearse

"The shared route carries forward the claim that loss of meeting meaning may create repeated rework or missed commitments for enterprise team leads. This is not a claim that automated summaries are needed."

Walk through each source without combining them:

  • Six constructed interviews: four leads report manual recap burden; two say ownership is usually settled during the meeting.
  • Thirty-one constructed support threads: the missing context tag mixes retrieval, permissions, and follow-through issues.
  • Constructed behavioral data: 42 percent of eligible meeting notes received an edit within 48 hours, but actor identity is missing for 18 percent.
  • A constructed pilot: the point estimate is +4.2 percentage points; the displayed plausible range is -0.8 to +9.1 points; the predeclared product target was +5 points.
"These sources are not votes. They have different populations, semantics, failure modes, and decision jobs."

Ask

"Which source feels most persuasive on first contact? Which limitation could most change that reaction?"

Take two quick reactions only.

Transition

"Before interpreting any of it, define what job the evidence is meant to perform."

Slide 4 - Decision-linked evidence chain

Time: 4 minutes Job: Carry the decision-first sequence into evidence planning.

Rehearse

"Reforge's decision-evidence fit argument is that evidence should be sufficient and relevant to the decision—not maximal. More evidence can be wasteful, and evidence that does not target the decision can create confidence without leverage."S2-SN-01

Move left to right:

"The decision is which Noted response to commit to. The weakest consequential claim is that loss of meeting meaning creates repeated material follow-through failure. Evidence must examine consequence, mechanism, prevalence, and alternatives. The action state is proceed, narrow, reframe, gather targeted evidence, or stop."
"Notice that the activity is still not selected. The claim and action states define the evidence job first."

Misconception recovery

If someone says every unknown should be researched:

"An unknown matters when resolving it could change the consequential choice. Curiosity is not the same as decision value."

Transition

"Now we can compare methods by what they can contribute to this job."

Slide 5 - Methods have different jobs

Time: 4 minutes Job: Prevent method prestige from becoming an evidence hierarchy.

Rehearse

"Reforge maps methods to different evidence needs and argues that fidelity comes from fit, audience, realism, existing evidence, sample, and layering—not simply more research."S2-SN-02

Walk the matrix:

"Interviews can expose mechanism, context, language, and workaround. They cannot estimate prevalence by themselves. Behavioral data can show pattern and magnitude, but cannot explain meaning. Usability testing can reveal interaction failure in a defined task, but not whether the broader problem matters. Surveys structure attitudes across a wider sample, but still report what people say. A controlled test can estimate a bounded treatment effect under valid design; it does not automatically explain the cause or predict durable production impact."
"Experimentation also has method constraints. Scale, decision timing, ethics, observability, interference, and reversibility can make a controlled test unsuitable even when causal identification would be attractive."S2-SN-03

Ask

"Which method on this slide would create the most information but the least decision value right now?"

Transition

"Method fit is not enough. If the metric is vague, the analysis can answer the wrong product question precisely."

Slide 6 - Metric meaning before measurement

Time: 4 minutes Job: Make metric semantics and altitude connection part of PM judgment.

Rehearse

"A metric name is shorthand. Before using it, define the behavior and value it represents, the actor, object, population, denominator, and window. Reforge's altitude material asks PMs to connect local solution behavior to product-area and company outcomes without assuming the connection is causal."S2-SN-04
"At solution altitude, we have confirmed follow-through within 48 hours. At product-area altitude, teams preserve and retrieve meeting meaning. At company altitude, enterprise teams retain Noted as trusted workflow infrastructure."
"The arrows are hypotheses. A confirmation click may represent administrative cleanup rather than meaningful follow-through. A local improvement may not affect retention. The connection must be credible, but it remains a model to test."

Misconception recovery

If someone says the metric is self-explanatory:

"Two teams can use the same label and capture different actors, triggers, denominators, or windows. The label is not the contract."

Transition

"Now inspect whether Noted can observe the behavior it just defined."

Slide 7 - Instrumentation sets the evidence ceiling

Time: 3 minutes Job: Show why a complete dashboard can still be unable to answer the claim.

Rehearse

"Reforge treats effective instrumentation as a prerequisite for reliable analysis. Event meaning, triggers, actors, objects, properties, and shared definitions determine what the data can represent."S2-SN-05

Walk the audit:

"The event fires on either open or edit, so it cannot establish confirmation. Actor identity is missing for 18 percent, weakening population comparisons. Meeting type is not captured, so the target context is invisible. Stable note and workspace IDs preserve some sequence."
"The responsible response is not to add a caveat after analysis and continue making the broad claim. We can weaken the claim, add another source, repair instrumentation, or defer."

Transition

"You now have enough to choose the evidence plan. The constraint is that no plan can repair every gap before the next cycle."

Slide 8 - Unit 4 decision

Time: 6 minutes individual work plus 8 minutes debrief Job: Produce a claim-linked evidence plan with a sufficiency boundary.

Give the instruction

"Start from the weakest consequential claim. Choose one evidence plan. Define the critical metric in product language. State what each source can and cannot establish, the material instrumentation boundary, and when the evidence becomes sufficient. Then name one attractive method you will not use. Six minutes."

At minute four:

"If your plan lists methods but no decision state, add the action the evidence could change. If your stopping rule is 'when we are confident,' name the condition."

Model debrief

After two learner responses:

"One defensible plan is to combine targeted interviews with a corrected behavioral cut. Interview recurring decision-heavy meeting leads who experienced both successful and failed follow-through. The interview can test the mechanism and consequence, not prevalence. Repair the event trigger and capture meeting type and actor coverage before using the behavior as confirmation."
"The evidence is sufficient for the next bounded decision when we can determine whether ownership handoff failure is repeated and material in the target context, and whether a meaningful behavioral pattern aligns with that mechanism. It is not sufficient to claim every enterprise team needs automated summaries."
"A broad survey is deliberately excluded now. It could quantify stated attitudes across a wider sample, but the current ambiguity is the mechanism and event meaning. A larger volume of ambiguous answers would not repair that."

Challenge weak answers

  • The method is chosen because it is considered rigorous rather than because it fits the claim.
  • The metric has no actor, denominator, or window.
  • Existing events are assumed valid because they appear in a dashboard.
  • The plan tries to answer mechanism, prevalence, causality, and durable value with one source.
  • The stopping rule requires certainty or agreement.
  • The excluded method is irrelevant rather than a real alternative.

Transition

"We have designed the evidence. Now we have to turn mixed observations into a belief without losing what makes them disagree."

Slide 9 - The synthesis ladder

Time: 5 minutes Job: Diagnose low-level and high-level synthesis traps.

Rehearse

"Reforge describes two synthesis traps. Low-level synthesis stays with quotes and observations and never produces a decision-relevant mechanism. High-level synthesis creates a clean theme without staying accountable to the research, exceptions, or segments."S2-SN-06

Walk the ladder:

"The atomic evidence is one lead saying they rewrite the action list. The observation is that four interviewed leads manually reconstruct follow-through. The pattern is that recap burden may emerge when ownership remains implicit. The belief update narrows the problem from missing summaries to unreliable ownership handoff."
"Every step increases usefulness and interpretive responsibility. The higher claim is not contained literally in the quote; it is a judgment that must remain traceable."

Ask

"Which rung is most often presented as an insight in your company?"

Transition

"A defensible synthesis does not climb once. It keeps moving in both directions."

Slide 10 - Bidirectional synthesis

Time: 4 minutes Job: Establish synthesis as a repeated evidence-belief loop.

Rehearse

"The hybrid discipline moves upward to patterns and mechanisms, pressure-tests alternatives and segments, traces important claims back down to evidence, then updates the decision state. Reforge's data-insight material similarly treats conjecture, planning, analysis, pressure testing, and update as a loop rather than a one-time readout."S2-SN-06S2-SN-07
"The current belief after this loop is that ownership handoff—not summary absence—may be the consequential mechanism. The phrase 'may be' is not weakness. It marks the current boundary."
"AI can accelerate retrieval, clustering, and contradiction checks. It can also make the majority pattern look cleaner than the evidence warrants. The PM remains accountable for semantic fidelity and omission."

Transition

"To make that accountability visible, put the support and contradiction beside the claim."

Slide 11 - Claim ledger

Time: 4 minutes Job: Make source lineage, contradiction, and segment boundary portable.

Rehearse

"The first claim—recap work is repeated—has support from four of six interviews and counterevidence from two leads who settle ownership during the meeting. The small selected sample limits the population claim."
"The second claim—consequence is material—is much weaker. Support threads mention missing context, but we do not have a verified missed-commitment rate, and the support tag mixes mechanisms."
"The pilot supports a positive observed difference, but the uncertainty spans harm, negligible value, and worthwhile value. Missing actor and meeting-type data weaken the target claim."
"The bounded update is therefore not 'meeting summaries are validated.' It is that ownership handoff is plausible for recurring decision-heavy meetings and deserves targeted investigation before a product commitment."

Ask

"Which claim changes most when the counterevidence is restored?"

Transition

"One remaining temptation is to treat any visible flaw as either fatal or irrelevant. Both are shortcuts."

Slide 12 - Four responses to flawed data

Time: 5 minutes Job: Make flaw response proportionate to decision consequence.

Rehearse

"Reforge's flawed-data material argues that relevant imperfect data can sometimes remain usable through partnership, workarounds, or explicit limits. The course adds the decision rule: the response depends on whether the defect threatens relevance, direction, magnitude, or population enough to reverse the consequential choice."S2-SN-08

Walk the four responses:

"Use with a boundary when the defect cannot reverse the narrow claim. Triangulate when a distinct source can test the same mechanism with different failure modes. Narrow or reframe when the evidence speaks only for one population or context. Stop or repair when the defect can reverse the decision and no responsible workaround exists."

Misconception recovery

If someone says all data is flawed:

"True as a general statement, useless as a decision rule. Name the defect, the claim it threatens, and whether it can change the action."

Transition

"Now make the belief update. A summary that changes no belief or decision is not complete."

Slide 13 - Unit 5 decision

Time: 6 minutes individual work plus 8 minutes debrief Job: Produce a traceable belief update with a genuine decision implication.

Give the instruction

"State the original conjecture, observation, interpretation, strongest counterevidence, material flaw, plausible alternative, and updated decision implication. Your update must strengthen, weaken, narrow, reframe, or leave the belief unchanged. Six minutes."

At minute four:

"Check whether your observation contains an explanation. Check whether your updated belief hides the two interviews that contradict it."

Model debrief

"Original conjecture: missing meeting summaries cause repeated enterprise follow-through failure. Observation: four of six interviewed leads manually reconstruct recaps, while two settle ownership during the meeting; support tags mix mechanisms; the behavioral metric is semantically incomplete."
"Interpretation: follow-through burden may be concentrated in recurring decision-heavy meetings where ownership remains implicit. Counterevidence: some teams resolve ownership without a summary. Material flaw: the event cannot identify meeting type and misses actors. Alternative explanation: retrieval or permissions, not ownership handoff, may drive the support pattern."
"Update: reframe and narrow. The evidence weakens the generic summary problem and strengthens a narrower ownership-handoff hypothesis. Decision implication: do not commit to automated summaries; obtain targeted mechanism evidence and repair the critical event semantics."

Challenge weak answers

  • The update restates the original belief with more evidence attached.
  • A repeated request is promoted directly to mechanism.
  • Contradiction is labeled an outlier without a reason.
  • The flaw appears as a footnote but does not change claim strength.
  • The belief becomes so narrow that it has no product consequence.
  • "We need more data" replaces a current decision state.

Transition to break

"We now have a bounded belief. After the break, we will interpret the pilot without treating its point estimate or threshold as the product answer."

Break - eight minutes

Restart exactly on time. Keep slide 13 visible during the break, then advance to slide 14.

Slide 14 - Observed estimate versus underlying effect

Time: 6 minutes Job: Separate what was observed from the effect the product decision concerns.

Rehearse

"The observed estimate is +4.2 percentage points. That is our sample estimate, not the effect Noted will realize. Reforge's true-versus-observed material uses repeated samples to show that observed values vary around an unknown underlying effect."S2-SN-09
"The displayed range spans -0.8 to +9.1 points. It contains small harm, negligible value, and worthwhile value. The predeclared product threshold was +5 points. The point estimate is positive and below the target; the range crosses zero and the target."
"Do not turn this into a probability statement about the hypothesis. A p-value does not measure the probability that the studied hypothesis is true, and statistical significance does not measure effect size or importance."S2-SN-10

Misconception recovery

If someone asks whether the true effect is likely +4.2:

"The point estimate is one estimate under this design. Its interpretation depends on the uncertainty procedure, assumptions, population, and integrity. It is not a guaranteed production effect."

Transition

"How much uncertainty is acceptable depends on what happens when we act wrongly in either direction."

Slide 15 - Error consequence matrix

Time: 6 minutes Job: Translate statistical error into product consequence.

Rehearse

"A false-positive product decision means proceeding when the underlying effect is not worthwhile. Noted would absorb integration, trust, and maintenance cost without earning enough value."
"A false-negative product decision means rejecting or indefinitely deferring a mechanism that is worthwhile. Material follow-through failure remains unresolved."
"Reducing one error can increase the other. The responsible threshold depends on consequence, reversibility, delay cost, exposure, and the value of targeted evidence. It should be considered before results are known."
"Statistical clarity does not create product significance. The +5 point threshold represents a product judgment about worthwhile value; it is not produced by the p-value."S2-SN-10

Ask

"Which error is more consequential here, and which assumption makes you say that?"

Take one answer and require the assumption.

Transition

"The threshold is necessary but still insufficient. We must inspect what happened before, during, and after the result."

Slide 16 - Three result-integrity gates

Time: 6 minutes Job: Prevent numerical precision from hiding design and interpretation failure.

Rehearse

"Before the result, the team declared a +5 point minimum worthwhile effect, workspace-level assignment, 14-day duration, and a trust guardrail. During execution, the dashboard was viewed at Day 7, but the team did not stop or extend. Cross-workspace contamination remains possible, and actor identity is incomplete."
"Afterward, the point estimate is below the target and the range crosses zero and the target. The high-complexity segment appears stronger, but that segment finding is exploratory. Production impact remains unknown."
"Repeated unplanned looks with conventional fixed-sample tests can change error risk and invite motivated stopping. If sequential monitoring is required, the method and rule need to be designed for it."S2-SN-11
"The result is inconclusive relative to the declared decision. That does not establish no effect. It also does not automatically justify extending the same test until the preferred threshold appears."S2-SN-12

Transition

"Make the action decision with the uncertainty still visible."

Slide 17 - Unit 6 decision

Time: 6 minutes individual work plus 8 minutes debrief Job: Produce a justified next action from an inconclusive result.

Give the instruction

"Interpret the observed estimate, minimum worthwhile effect, uncertainty, design concern, false-positive and false-negative consequence, segment signal, and production boundary. Choose proceed, stage, gather targeted evidence, reframe, or stop. Six minutes."

At minute four:

"If your answer is 'run longer,' state which unresolved decision-relevant uncertainty more time would answer and why the analysis remains valid."

Model debrief

"One defensible action is gather targeted evidence and reframe. The observed estimate is positive but below the product threshold; the displayed range remains compatible with harm, negligible value, and worthwhile value. The design has actor missingness and possible cross-workspace contamination. The stronger high-complexity segment is exploratory."
"The false-positive consequence is building and owning weak value. The false-negative consequence is leaving material follow-through failure unresolved. Because the mechanism evidence already narrowed toward ownership handoff, the next move should not be a generic extension. Repair observability and run a bounded follow-up focused on recurring high-complexity meetings, with a predeclared decision rule and contamination review."
"This is not a disguised proceed decision. Automated summaries remain uncommitted. The pilot changed the decision by narrowing the population and next evidence job."

Acceptable alternatives

A staged move can be defensible if exposure, rollback, population, guardrails, and learning value are explicit. Stop can be defensible if lifecycle cost is high and the false-negative consequence is limited. Challenge answers that:

  • treat +4.2 points as the true effect;
  • treat the missed threshold as proof of no effect;
  • use the exploratory segment as a confirmed finding;
  • ignore the minimum worthwhile effect;
  • authorize full launch from a narrow pilot;
  • continue until significance without a valid sequential plan.

Transition

"We can now assemble the Week 2 record. The deliverable is the path from claim to changed decision."

Slide 18 - The Week 2 Evidence and Belief Update

Time: 7 minutes Job: Convert the session into one inspectable capstone checkpoint.

Rehearse

"The Week 2 artifact begins with the decision-linked claim. It records the evidence plan, what each source can and cannot establish, metric meaning, observability, and sufficiency."
"It then shows the traceable synthesis: observations, abstraction, counterevidence, segment, known flaw, alternative explanation, and genuine belief update."
"Finally, it records the measurement boundary: estimate, product threshold, error consequence, integrity, product significance, and justified action."
"Do not attach a research report, analytics screenshot, and experiment readout as three finished artifacts. If they do not resolve into one changed decision state, the evidence cycle is incomplete."

Explain the after-session work

Learners spend approximately 75 minutes updating their Product Decision Case in their own product context or in Noted, followed by the weekly 15-minute owner check-in.

Ask only:

  1. Which evidence source had the most important decision job?
  2. What is the strongest limit or contradiction in the current belief?
  3. How did the decision change—and what belief is being handed to strategy?

Do not edit the evidence packet. Diagnose the reasoning chain.

Transition

"Evidence becomes strategically useful only when it constrains the story the product is allowed to tell."

Slide 19 - Handoff to Session 3

Time: 4 minutes plus 7 minutes open Q&A Job: Close Session 2 and protect the strategic handoff.

Rehearse

"Session 3 will not build strategy from the raw evidence packet. It will start from the calibrated belief: what the evidence supports, contradicts, and cannot establish."
"The next weakest link may no longer be the user problem. It may be the advantage, growth path, economics, portfolio allocation, or lifecycle consequence of a technical option."
"Bring one current belief, one decision state, and the condition most capable of changing direction. Do not bring a longer list of everything we still do not know."

Final check

Ask learners to complete:

"The belief I am carrying forward is ____. The evidence boundary strategy must respect is ____."

Open Q&A boundary

Use the final seven minutes for evidence and interpretation principles. Move calculation, test-design, or company-specific analytics questions into the check-in or specialist review.

Close with:

"Good evidence does not remove judgment. It makes the judgment accountable to what the world was capable of telling us."

Facilitation diagnostics

If learners want a universal evidence hierarchy

Say:

"Evidence strength is claim- and decision-dependent. A valid experiment can answer a narrow treatment question better than an interview; an interview can expose a mechanism the experiment cannot. Name the job before ranking the source."

If learners keep adding methods

Ask:

"Which additional decision state becomes available because of this source? If none, why are we collecting it?"

If the room confuses synthesis with summarization

Return to Slide 9 and ask for one movement upward and one movement downward. Require the learner to name the observation and the interpretation separately.

If learners become statistics-anxious

Say:

"You are not being tested on formula recall. Supervise the claim: what was observed, what remains possible, what was declared before the result, which error matters, and what action is justified."

If learners want a canonical Noted answer

Say:

"Stage, gather targeted evidence, reframe, or stop can all be defensible. The quality test is whether the action respects the product threshold, design integrity, evidence boundary, and consequence of both errors."

If time is running short

Protect, in order:

  1. all three six-minute decisions;
  2. the Unit 6 debrief;
  3. the Week 2 handoff;
  4. direct Q&A.

Compress examples on slides 5, 11, and 15. Do not skip the instrumentation audit, the observed-versus-underlying distinction, or the provenance statement.
